_meta.description: Tamil Nadu district & sessions court formatting rules — drives cause-title, party designations, prayer language, verification format
_meta.change_protocol: CLO sign-off required for any change. Vishal raises Jira tickets to Ajay for additions; never edits unilaterally.

designation: IN THE COURT OF PRINCIPAL DISTRICT & SESSIONS JUDGE
jurisdictionNote: District-level criminal and civil courts in Tamil Nadu. Sessions courts try offences punishable with imprisonment exceeding 7 years. Sessions cases are typically numbered S.C. No. and special sessions cases as Spl. Sessions C. No. Chennai operates as the City Civil & Sessions Court under the Tamil Nadu Civil Courts Act, 1873 and the Madras High Court Original Side Rules as locally adapted.

party_designation.state: State of Tamil Nadu represented by the Public Prosecutor / Inspector of Police (as applicable) through the Principal Secretary, Home Department, Government of Tamil Nadu, Chennai

prayer_language.opening: It is, therefore, most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to:
prayer_language.closing: And for this act of kindness, the petitioner shall, as in duty bound, ever pray.

verification_format:
I, {deponent_name}, {designation}, do hereby solemnly affirm and declare that the contents of the above petition from paragraph ___ to paragraph ___ are true to my personal knowledge and the contents of paragraphs ___ to ___ are believed to be true on the basis of information received and legal advice tendered, which I believe to be true. Nothing material has been concealed therefrom.

Solemnly affirmed at {place} on this {date}.

DEPONENT
localRules: Bail applications under S.483 BNSS must disclose any earlier rejection by the Magistrate or any co-ordinate court.
Anticipatory bail applications (S.482 BNSS) in Tamil Nadu are typically presented before the Sessions Court / High Court with affidavit, FIR copy and proof of jurisdiction.

Vakalatnama in the form prescribed under the Madras High Court Original Side / Appellate Side Rules and the Tamil Nadu Civil Rules of Practice to be filed at the first instance with the requisite court-fee stamp.
All civil pleadings to be paginated, indexed and accompanied by a list of documents under Order VII / Order VIII CPC.
Tamil translation may be insisted upon for documents in English where parties are not conversant; cf. Tamil Nadu Official Language Act, 1956 and the Tamil Nadu Civil Rules of Practice.
In Chennai, plaints before the City Civil Court are valued under the Tamil Nadu Civil Courts Act, 1873 as amended; pecuniary limits periodically revised by State Govt. notification.
Service of summons in Chennai is supplemented by registered post AD under the Tamil Nadu Civil Rules of Practice.
Atrocities (SC/ST) cases, POCSO cases and NDPS cases are tried by designated Special Courts notified by the State Government.
e_filing_note: e-Filing is operational at Madras HC and Chennai City Civil Court and select district HQs via the eCourts portal; not yet mandatory state-wide.
